confirmed_findings.summary: move_item guards only the SOURCE against the federation boundary (guard_no_foreign_library_under(&app, &source_path)) and applies no guard at all to target_folder, while validate_path_in_any_library and the Move picker both resolve the FEDERATED library set — so a note or folder can be silently relocated out of the active universe and into a LINKED universe's library, and the active universe's index then permanently indexes a file it does not own.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Universe A has a cUniverse child B linked, both on the same volume. list_universe_folders (libraries.rs:2721) builds its list from load_all_libraries — the federated resolver — and the frontend renders B's libraries as first-class destinations (buildUniverseFolderEntries in +layout.svelte assigns them iconKind 'cuniverse' with a planet icon). The user right-clicks 'Research.md' in Universe A, chooses Move to…, and picks a folder inside B. move_item runs: validate_path_in_any_library(&app, &target_folder) succeeds because it iterates the federated set (libraries.rs:654); guard_no_foreign_library_under is called ONLY on source_path (2572) so nothing objects; gate_rename succeeds (same volume). The command returns Ok(dest). move_item_db_tail then calls library_name_for_path(load_all_libraries(app), new_path) — which resolves to B's library — and migrate_note_db_paths + reindex_single_note write the note's row into A's search.db under B's library_name at a path inside B's directory. Result, with no error anywhere: (a) the .md file has physically left the user's universe and now lives inside another knowledge base's tree; (b) A's index holds a row for a file under a foreign root — exactly the Charter W2-9 class PJ-207 §8 removed elsewhere; (c) boot reconcile can never heal it, because reconcile::run skips every row whose path is under no OWN root (`if !roots_norm.iter().any(|r| under(&pn, r)) { … continue; }`, reconcile.rs ~line 340) and merely counts it as foreign_rows; (d) if the user later unlinks cUniverse B, the note is gone from A with a stale index row still serving its old text in search and backlinks. Worse for a FOLDER move: retarget_registered_libraries(&app, &source_path, Some(&dest_str)) at 2584 rewrites A's OWN libraries.json to point a registered library at a path inside B's directory, so two universes' registries now claim the same folder.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified end-to-end in source. move_item (libraries.rs:2544-2600) applies guard_no_foreign_library_under to source_path ONLY (2572) and no own-universe/root guard to target_folder; validate_path_in_any_library (:653) authorizes via load_all_libraries, the FEDERATED resolver, so a folder inside a linked cUniverse passes. The path is reachable: list_universe_folders (:2720) walks the federated set and buildUniverseFolderEntries (+layout.svelte:6891-6931) renders linked-universe libraries as first-class destinations (iconKind 'cuniverse'); openMoveDialog filters only self/descendants/current-parent. The identical defect in the sibling Ctrl+N picker was fixed 2026-08-10 (commit 453a91c2, ownUniverseLibraries at +layout.svelte:1623, ruling "universe-wide is right for RESOLVING a name, wrong for CHOOSING where to write") — the Move picker was not, a Whole-Ecosystem Fix Law gap. MoveDialog.svelte:4 asserts the guard exists ("move_item rejects cross-library/outside-universe targets anyway") — it does not; the assumption is documented, the enforcement is absent (LL-023 drift). move_item_db_tail (:2620-2665) then resolves library_name_for_path against the federated list and writes A's search.db row under B's library name at a path inside B's root. The resulting divergence is permanently silent: reconcile::run draws roots from try_load_libraries (own only, reconcile.rs:268), continues past any row outside them (:345) counting it as foreign_rows, and has_findings deliberately excludes foreign_rows (proven by its own test at reconcile.rs:1081) — never healed, never reported. Unlink B later and the row is not even counted, leaving stale text served in search and backlinks forever. Folder case is worse: retarget_registered_libraries (:535-567) rewrites A's libraries.json to a path under B's root, the exact state ensure_under_active_root (:725, enforced in add_library :747 and create_new_library_at :3624) exists to forbid. add_child_universe (universe.rs:1453) imposes no under-root constraint, so B is genuinely outside A. Refutations attempted and failed: gate_rename is a plain locked fs::rename with no boundary check; the reindex error path logs but the success path is the defect; no trigger, version-gate, or reconcile pass corrects it; the user's click is explicit but every consequence (note left the universe, foreign index row, registry pointing outside the root) is unsurfaced. Not APP-KILLER because it requires an opt-in cUniverse link plus a deliberate foreign destination pick and the .md bytes survive intact under B — the loss is A's ownership, registry integrity, and index truth.

confirmed_findings.summary: The write-ahead crash-recovery net is mirrored into a single unbounded, never-pruned localStorage blob and the setItem is wrapped in an empty catch, so once the origin quota is reached the net silently stops persisting across restarts.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: `setWriteAhead` (store.ts:353-360) keeps the whole net in ONE key (`constellation-wab`) as `{path: {content, ...}}` and re-serializes it on every stash; a QuotaExceededError is swallowed by the bare `catch {}` on line 360. The blob is never pruned or capped, and it grows on ordinary READING: NoteEditor.svelte:427 stashes a full-content snapshot entry on every editor teardown (the `!needsDiskSave` branch — tab switch, {#key} remount, close), and closeTab (store.ts:3824-3847) deliberately does NOT clear it; only re-opening that same note consumes it (resolveNoteContent, store.ts:3171). On the Boss's universe (~7,820 notes / 298 MB, i.e. ~38 KB average note) roughly 130 distinct notes browsed in one session fills a 5 MB Chromium origin quota. From that moment every stash — including the 'net BEFORE the write' stash the entire Save-Durability contract depends on (noteSession.ts:243) — throws and is discarded. The in-memory Map still answers, so nothing looks wrong: no banner, no console error, no journal line. The user then hits a failed save (locked .md / AV / synced folder) and the app crashes or is killed; on relaunch the recovery copy getWriteAhead was supposed to return is absent from localStorage and the edit exists nowhere — the exact loss the net was built to prevent, with the net reporting nothing. store.ts:314-319 already names this exposure ('never pruned or capped, and setWriteAhead swallows a quota exception with an empty catch') but no cap, prune or surface was ever added.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in code and against real data. store.ts:340-361 mirrors the WHOLE write-ahead net into a single localStorage key (WAB_LS_KEY, :332) by read-modify-write, with the setItem in a bare `catch {}` (:356-360). Grep of src/ finds only five WAB_LS_KEY sites (set/get/clear + the rename migration) — no cap, no prune, no eviction, no boot sweep; the file's own comment at :314-319 already names the exposure, and the PJ-229 fix at UniverseSetup.svelte:299-315 confirms the key is deliberately preserved, never swept. The blob grows on READING: NoteEditor.svelte:427 (the !needsDiskSave teardown branch) stashes a merely-viewed note's full composed content on every teardown (tab switch, {#key} remount, close); closeTab (store.ts:3830-3860) does not clear it; the only consumer is resolveNoteContent's clearWriteAhead on reopen (:3178), whose teardown immediately re-stashes. So the key set trends monotonically toward every note ever opened and survives restarts. Reachability measured, not assumed: the Boss's universe (E:\Constellation Universes\Eisa Cognitive Knowledge) is 8,060 notes / 299.5 MB / mean 38.05 KB / median 22.5 KB — against a 5-10 MB Chromium/WebView2 origin quota that is ~230-450 distinct notes browsed, i.e. days of ordinary reading. Past that point every stash silently loses its durable half while the in-memory Map (:353) keeps answering, so nothing observable changes: no banner, no console.warn (contrast resolveNoteContent:3147, which does warn), no saveHealth entry. This includes the contract's "NET BEFORE THE WRITE" (noteSession.ts:255-256 via standardSaveEnv's setNet: setWriteAhead, store.ts:500). The localStorage net is the ONLY cross-restart copy of unsaved bytes — session.json is paths/arrangement only, explicitly "never note content" (session.ts:56-58). Concrete failure: user has browsed enough notes to fill the quota (silent) -> a save fails under a file lock/AV/sync (banner shown, model dirty, net "retained" per contract) -> hard kill/crash -> on relaunch getWriteAhead returns nothing and the edit exists nowhere, with no error at any point. Refutations attempted and defeated: nothing prunes or caps; the failed setItem leaves the stale blob intact so it never self-heals; the durability gate's onError/save-health surfaces the WRITE failure, never the net-stash failure; reopening notes cannot shrink the blob because teardown re-stashes.

confirmed_findings.summary: The watcher flush drains pendingTabReloads/pendingReindex into locals BEFORE a run of unguarded awaits, so one rejected read_library_tree aborts the async callback and the whole batch of external changes is dropped with no adopt, no reindex and no requeue.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: scheduleWatcherFlush's `setTimeout(async () => {...}, 300)` (+layout.svelte:3656) copies and then CLEARS all three pending sets on lines 3663-3666, and the callback body has no try/catch. The first work it does is `for (const vid of libraryIds) await refreshLibraryTree(vid)` (line 3671) — an unguarded `await invoke('read_library_tree', ...)` (+layout.svelte:7614) whose command returns Err("Library path does not exist.") (libraries.rs:826) or Err("Access denied: not a registered library.") (libraries.rs:822). Concretely: two libraries change inside the same 300 ms window, one of them a federated cUniverse library on a removable/network volume that is momentarily unavailable (or a folder deleted externally — itself a watcher-firing event). The loop rejects on that library and the callback's promise rejects as an unhandled rejection nobody observes. Because the drain already happened, the OTHER library's changed paths are gone from pendingReindex and pendingTabReloads: adoptExternalChangeIntoTabs (line 3684) never runs, so an open CLEAN tab keeps the pre-edit body on screen and its next debounced save durably writes that stale body over the external edit (silent content loss, the PJ-070 clobber shape); reindex_changed_paths (line 3713) never runs, so note_meta/FTS stay stale; and the bounded requeue at line 3700 is unreachable because it lives inside the catch of an invoke that was never issued. Nothing is logged and nothing re-fires — the watcher will not emit again for those files.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in source. scheduleWatcherFlush (+layout.svelte:3658-3664) drains and CLEARS pendingTreeRefresh/pendingTabReloads/pendingReindex into locals, then runs `for (const vid of libraryIds) await refreshLibraryTree(vid)` (3670-3672) with no try/catch anywhere in the async callback. refreshLibraryTree (7611-7618) awaits a bare invoke('read_library_tree'), which returns Err at libraries.rs:822 ("Access denied: not a registered library.") and :826 ("Library path does not exist."). A rejection there aborts the callback before adoptExternalChangeIntoTabs (3682) and before the reindex block (3693); the PJ-187 bounded requeue at 3700 is unreachable because it sits inside the catch of an invoke that was never issued. The whole batch of external changes is discarded. Silence confirmed: handleUnhandledRejection (3230-3233) is console.error + e.preventDefault(), and devtools are disabled in release builds. No recovery: openNoteTab early-returns on an already-open path (3228/3248) without re-reading disk, so the un-adopted CLEAN tab keeps its pre-change body until restart; the main save path invoke('write_note', {filePath, content, origin}) (store.ts:2910) passes NO `expect`, so gate_write takes the OkUnchecked route and the stale body overwrites the external edit with no CAS refusal and no .conflict sidecar (the dirty-conflict branch is unreachable for a clean model). Reachability corrected from the candidate: the "removable/network volume unavailable" path does NOT fire (notify hands the closure an Err, dropped by `if let Ok(event)` at watcher.rs:82 — no emit). The reachable triggers are (1) a registered library DIRECTORY removed/renamed externally under the Universe root (git pull / Syncthing / Explorer) — the watcher deliberately passes vanished paths (watcher.rs:86-94), so that library id enters pendingTreeRefresh and read_library_tree Errs "Library path does not exist", dropping every other changed path in the same 300ms batch; and (2) the universe-switch window where set_active_universe has flipped but $libraryStats still holds the departing universe's libraries (handleUniverseSwitch, 3089-3107) — the exact rejection shape libraries.rs:900-903 records as a real past incident. Partial mitigation found: the missed reindex IS surfaced at next launch — reconcile::maybe_schedule (reconcile.rs:224-248) counts the file as `drifted` via the PJ-207 §9 mtime comparison and feeds index_repair::record_drift_report (the drift notice + "Repair now"). So the index-divergence half is bounded and visible; the missed adopt half is not (no retry, no re-emit, no write-time freshness attestation), leaving a genuine silent overwrite of external content. Contrast with the same block's own hardening — "a deleted file's rejection is caught per-path so it can't sink the batch (invariant #8)" and PJ-187's requeue — and with the guarded call sites at 5120 and 7590 confirms this is an oversight, not a design. Fix: per-id try/catch, or a try/finally that requeues tabPaths/reindexPaths on throw.

confirmed_findings.summary: A pending (debounced) property edit is silently discarded on a tab switch: the seed `$effect` FORCE-re-seeds `editableProps` whenever `tabChanged`, overwriting the un-committed rows, while the teardown flush that the code comment claims covers this case is itself skipped by its live-identity gate.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: The right-sidebar Properties panel (+layout.svelte:9731) is mounted with `tabId={sidebarTab.id}` where `sidebarTab = $derived($focusedTab)` (+layout.svelte:1631) and with NO `{#key}` — it survives tab switches. The user edits a property value (e.g. changes `stage`), which sets `editableProps` and arms the 800 ms `saveTimeout` (PropertyEditor.svelte:1066-1067). Nothing has reached the model yet — the intents only run inside `commitAndSave`. Within 800 ms the user clicks another tab. The seed `$effect` fires with `tabChanged === true`, and its condition `if ((!saving && !localEditPending) || tabChanged)` (line 457) deliberately BYPASSES the `localEditPending` protection, so `editableProps`/`seededRows` are replaced with the NEW note's rows and `seededForPath = filePath` is set to the NEW path (line 458). The still-armed timer then fires `commitAndSave(tabId, filePath)` (line 1079) against the NEW note: `rowsBelongToTarget` passes (seededForPath now equals the new path), `plan` diffs the freshly-seeded rows against the same model, yields nothing, and `if (!changed && !isNoteDirty(id)) return` (line 1047) exits. The old note's edit reached neither the model, the disk, nor the write-ahead net; no banner, no `commitRefused`, no console error. The comment at line 454-455 asserts "A tab change always re-seeds — that is a different note, and its pending edit is flushed by the teardown path" — but this instance has no teardown on a tab switch, and the EMBEDDED panel (NotePane.svelte:1712), which IS destroyed by the `{#key}`, skips its onDestroy flush too because its gate `tabId === mountedTabId && filePath === mountedFilePath` (line 629) reads the already-updated live props. Both panels drop it. Distinct from the filed PJ-187 in-place-nav drop (same tab id, new path), which is refused by `rowsBelongToTarget` and is documented at line 986-990; this is the different-tab-id path, which the code believes is handled.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in source, not inferred. (1) The right-sidebar Properties panel (+layout.svelte:9726-9747) is mounted with tabId={sidebarTab.id} / sidebarTab = $derived($focusedTab) (line 1631) and NO {#key} — the only {#key} in the file is at 9241 around FocusPane — so the instance survives a tab switch and merely re-points. (2) All property mutation sites (updateValue:715, removeProperty:732, setType, applyTaxonomySelection, toggleCheckbox …) only write local $state and call debouncedSave(); editPropValue/addPropTo/removePropFrom are called ONLY inside commitAndSave (line 1021), and the tab.content mutation now also lives inside commitAndSave (PJ-207 §15). For the whole 800 ms window the edit exists nowhere but editableProps — not the model, not tab.content, not the write-ahead net. (3) The seed $effect at line 457 — `if ((!saving && !localEditPending) || tabChanged)` — deliberately bypasses the pending-edit guard on a tab change, overwrites editableProps/seededRows with the new note's rows and sets seededForPath = the NEW filePath (458). The armed timer is not cleared (clearTimeout appears only at 612 and 1066). (4) The timer then fires commitAndSave(tabId, filePath) against the new note: rowsBelongToTarget passes (seededForPath now equals the new path), plan diffs the freshly-seeded rows against the same model, changed === false, and line 1047 returns. No commitRefused banner, no console.error, no error anywhere. (5) The comment at 454-455 claiming the teardown path covers this is false for BOTH instances: the sidebar instance has no teardown on a tab switch, and the embedded instance (NotePane.svelte:1712 inside NoteEditor.svelte:773's {#key}) skips its onDestroy flush because its gate (line 629) compares the MOUNT snapshots against LIVE tabId/filePath, which the file's own Sweep-2026-07-18 #1 note (lines 616-624) documents as already pointing at the incoming note at teardown. Refutations attempted and eliminated: no blur/change commit exists (every field is oninput → debouncedSave, lines 1164-1419), so clicking the tab bar blurs without flushing; PropertyEditor exports only addProperty/removeProperty, so no host can flush it; flushOutgoing/flushIfDirty flush the MODEL, which never received the edit — PJ-187's own comment concedes panel-level flush at navigation is "filed", i.e. unbuilt; PROPS_SINGLE_OWNERSHIP and SINGLE_OWNERSHIP are both true, so the model-read path is live. Reachable by an ordinary gesture: toggle a checkbox / delete a property row / pick taxonomy pills, then click another tab within 800 ms — the edit is discarded silently and the note keeps its pre-edit value on disk. Blast radius is bounded (the re-seed prevents the old rows landing on the new note, so no cross-note corruption; only the last un-committed edit is lost, which is why this is HIGH and not APP-KILLER), but the loss is real, silent, non-self-correcting, and the code believes it is handled.

confirmed_findings.summary: `update_frontmatter_title` escapes only `"` (never `\`) when re-emitting the OLD title into `aliases:`, and `extract_frontmatter_title` (line 2166) strips quotes WITHOUT decoding escapes — so a rename re-escapes an already-escaped title and emits frontmatter that no longer parses.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Create a note titled `He said "hi"`. `create_note` (libraries.rs:1284) writes VALID frontmatter: `title: "He said \"hi\""`. Now rename the note. `extract_frontmatter_title` returns `He said \"hi\"` (trim_matches strips only the OUTER quotes; the backslashes survive as data). `esc_old` then doubles them and line 2264/2306 emits `  - "He said \\"hi\\""`. Verified against the app's own `yaml` parser: 1 error, `Unexpected scalar at node end`. The note's ENTIRE frontmatter is now unparseable. From that moment `frontmatterIsRewritable` is false, `composeFrontmatter`'s H1 branch re-emits the bytes verbatim, and the closed-note tag path (`+layout.svelte:7079` → `composeUpdatedContent`) writes the file back, resolves cleanly and `addTagToNote` returns `true` — a false success with nothing written. The old title is also lost from `aliases`, so every `[[old title]]` wikilink silently stops resolving. Same emitter also breaks on a plain backslash: `title: "A\Users\x" ` → `Invalid escape sequence` (verified), and `title: "a\b"` parses SUCCESSFULLY to `a` + U+0008 — a silently different title. Contrast `bases.rs::format_yaml_value`, which correctly does `.replace('\\', "\\\\").replace('"', "\\\"")`.
confirmed_findings.reason: Reproduced by reading the code and running the emission through the app's own `yaml` parser. `extract_frontmatter_title` (libraries.rs:2166) strips quotes with `trim_matches('\"')` and decodes NO escapes, so for the valid on-disk line `title: \"He said \\\"hi\\\"\"` it returns the raw bytes `He said \\\"hi\\` (backslashes survive as data; the escaped closing quote is consumed as a delimiter). `update_frontmatter_title` then re-escapes with `esc_old = old_title.replace('\"', \"\\\\\\\"\")` (line 2176) and emits `  - \"He said \\\\\"hi\\\"` at 2249/2278/2307/2316. Verified with parseDocument (the same call `frontmatterIsRewritable` makes): the pre-rename frontmatter has 0 errors, the post-rename frontmatter has 1 error — `Unexpected scalar at node end`. The note's .md on disk (the source of truth) now carries unparseable frontmatter, and the old title is destroyed rather than preserved as an alias. Reachable through normal UI with no import needed: QuickSwitcher.svelte:127 builds the create row from the raw query and +layout.svelte:5920 passes it straight to createNote with NO illegal-char validation (the `ILLEGAL_CHARS_RE` guard exists only in CreateItemDialog.svelte:82); NoteEditor.svelte:764 (unresolved-wikilink create) is likewise unguarded; and create_note (libraries.rs:1283) deliberately keeps the raw user title in frontmatter while sanitizing only the filename, so a quote-bearing title is an anticipated on-disk shape. No aliases block is required — the `!found_aliases` branch (2314-2316) emits the same broken line, as does the inline-array branch (2275, whose `split_flow_seq_items`/`unquote_one_pair` also strips one quote pair without decoding escapes). Nothing surfaces an error at the moment of corruption: rename_item returns Ok and its DB tail is detached/best-effort. Downstream, composeFrontmatter's H1 gate (yamlDoc.ts:465) passes malformed bytes through verbatim, so the closed-note tag path (+layout.svelte:7079 -> composeUpdatedContent) writes the file back unchanged and addTagToNote returns `true` — a false success. Partial refutation that does not save the candidate: the OPEN-note property path IS surfaced (frontmatterIsRewritable -> propsAreWritable -> the PJ-187 banner), so only the closed-note tag/link writes false-succeed. Confirmed companion of the same missing-`\\`-escape class: create_note:1283 and store.ts:2807 `quoteIfNeeded` escape only `\"`, so `title: \"A\\Users\\x\"` is written INVALID at creation (`Invalid escape sequence`, verified) and `title: \"a\\b\"` parses silently to `a`+U+0008 — a different title than the user typed. bases.rs::format_yaml_value already does the correct `.replace('\\\\', ...)` then `.replace('\"', ...)`, so the right pattern exists in-tree.

confirmed_findings.summary: The Expression Forge builds a new note's frontmatter by raw string interpolation — `title: "${compositionTitle.trim()}"` — with no quoting or escaping at all, so a title containing a double quote produces a note born with frontmatter that does not parse.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: In the Expression Forge, name a composition `The "Real" Thing` and export. The filename is sanitized (`replace(/[<>:"/\\|?*]/g,'_')` on line 137) but the TITLE is interpolated raw, producing `title: "The "Real" Thing"`. Verified with the app's `yaml` parser: 1 error, `Unexpected scalar at node end at line 1, column 14`. `createNote` + `writeNote` + `reindexNote` all succeed with no error surfaced; the user sees a normal new note. Its property block is dead from birth: `parseFrontmatter` falls back to the line scanner, `frontmatterIsRewritable` returns false, and every later property intent on that note is refused or (via the closed-note paths) silently discarded by `composeFrontmatter`'s H1 passthrough. This is exactly the class PJ-187 exported `quoteIfNeeded` for ("two other places were hand-building a `key: value` frontmatter line by concatenation") — this is a third site the sweep missed.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified at ExpressionForge.svelte:136-144: the filename is sanitized (`/[<>:\"/\\|?*]/`) but the title is interpolated raw into a double-quoted YAML scalar. Ran the app's own `yaml` parser on the exact emitted bytes: `title: \"The \"Real\" Thing\"` → 1 error (`Unexpected scalar at node end`, title reads back as `The `), and `title: \"C:\\Users\\notes\"` → 1 error (`Invalid escape sequence \\Users\\not`). Both characters are legal in a composition title (the sanitizer's own char class proves the code expects them). The path is reachable: ExpressionForge is mounted at +layout.svelte:9109, toggled by the ungated command-palette entry `expression-forge` (line 2571), and `compositionTitle` is a free-text bound input (line 158). Nothing surfaces at birth: Rust `write_note` validates only path/filename (no YAML check), `createNote`/`writeNote` resolve, `reindexNote` only logs. The note is then permanently un-property-writable — noteModel.ts:163 → frontmatterIsRewritable (yamlDoc.ts:419) is false on `doc.errors.length > 0`, and composeFrontmatter's H1 branch (yamlDoc.ts:464) re-emits the frontmatter verbatim. The open-editor half IS surfaced (propsAreWritable → PropertyEditor.svelte:1102 banner), but the closed-note paths are not: composeUpdatedContent (store.ts:2900) feeds the same H1 branch for add_tag (+layout.svelte:7079), reviewer_connect (store.ts:1562) and link_mention (store.ts:1643) — writeNote succeeds while the tag/link intent is silently discarded, the exact false-success yamlDoc.ts:410 calls catastrophic. Third site of the class PJ-187 exported quoteIfNeeded for (rebrandCopyFrontmatter + the +layout.svelte:4802 template merge were the two it fixed). Not APP-KILLER: no body content is lost (the fence closes, body preserved) and the YAML is hand-repairable in the editor. Adjacent defect found while verifying: quoteIfNeeded (store.ts:2791) does not escape backslashes, so routing this site through it fixes the quote case but not `C:\\Users\\notes` — the quoter needs `\\\\` escaping as part of the fix.

confirmed_findings.summary: `update_base_columns` (and its twin `update_base_order` at :421, plus `save_workspace_base` at bases.rs:769 and the creates at bases.rs:362/733) rewrites the user's sole-copy `.base` file with a plain `std::fs::write` — truncate-then-write, no temp file, no fsync — the exact shape PJ-207 §15 eliminated for `.canvas` and 2026-08-03 eliminated for style-presets.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: User opens a Base and clicks a column header to sort (BaseTab `cycleSort` → `persistOrder` → `update_base_order`). Rust reads the .base, re-serializes the whole LensDefinition, and calls `std::fs::write(&file_path, &yaml)`, which opens the file with O_TRUNC. The machine loses power / the process is killed / an AV or sync client faults the write after the truncate but before the bytes land — or the write returns Ok with the data still in page cache and the machine dies before writeback (there is no `sync_all` anywhere on this path). The `.base` is now zero-length or half-YAML. Nothing is reported at the time: no error, no banner, the click looked like it worked. The next open calls `parse_lens_yaml`, which fails, and the saved view — its scope, filters, columns and sort, the only copy of it anywhere (no .prev, no SQLite mirror, no .trash copy) — is gone with nothing on screen able to say why. Header clicks are a per-interaction write, so the truncate window is opened dozens of times per session per base.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified by reading the code end to end. Reachable per-interaction path: BaseTab.svelte:160 cycleSort -> :169 persistOrder -> store.ts:108 invoke('update_base_order') -> lens/query.rs:405-423, which ends in a bare `std::fs::write(&file_path, &yaml)` at :421 (same at :393 for update_base_columns, and bases.rs:312/362/733/769). Truncate-then-write, no temp file, no sync_all. The alphabet rail (BaseTab.svelte:459) fires persistOrder automatically too. Refutations all fail: (1) not durable — universe::atomic_write (universe.rs:186-212, temp + sync_all + rename) is the project's writer and none of these six sites call it; (2) no second copy — grep shows no SQLite mirror, no .prev, no .trash copy for .base, so the file is the sole copy of the saved view's scope/filters/columns/order; (3) not surfaced — an Ok-returning write whose bytes never reach disk raises nothing, and the resulting zero-length .base makes read_note return '', so BaseTab.svelte:97 (`if (!y.trim()) return;`) bails BEFORE clearing `loading`, leaving the template at :522 rendering 'Loading…' permanently — not the error branch, not the legacy branch. The saveError catch at :175 only sees Err returns and never fires. confirmed_findings.summary: The onDestroy pending-save flush is gated on MOUNT-time identity snapshots (`mountedTabId`/`mountedFilePath`, captured once at lines 82–83), which for the never-remounted right-sidebar instance stay pinned to the first note ever shown — so after the first note switch the teardown flush is permanently dead and a pending property edit is silently dropped on panel close.

The edit is discarded: nothing on disk, nothing in the model, no console output (the gate's skip is silent by design — it was written for the `{#key}`-remounted NotePane instance, where the snapshot is always the current note). confirmed_findings.summary: The cross-library wikilink resolver holds the app-wide read_db mutex across an unbounded, no-early-exit recursive filesystem walk of the library — every other read command in the app parks for its duration.

For those seconds every reader command is blocked on the same mutex: get_backlink_rows (cache.rs:636), get_outgoing_rows (cache.rs:674), get_structural_children/ancestors/descendants (structural.rs:237/257/296), scan_unlinked_mentions (libraries.rs:3993), and the rename cascade's own candidate seek (libraries.rs:6688). confirmed_findings.summary: The NotePane teardown flush is gated on the LIVE `tab.path`, so on a TAB SWITCH (different tab id) the outgoing editor's onDestroy flush is dropped entirely — no disk write, and critically no `setWriteAhead` crash-recovery stash — leaving the edits only in volatile memory with no timer left to persist them.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Tab A and tab B are open (non-split). The user types a paragraph in tab A and, within the 1500 ms debounce, clicks tab B in the tab bar. `switchTab` sets `activeTabId`; `+layout.svelte:9383` mounts `<NoteEditor tab={$activeTab}>` with NO outer key, so NoteEditor persists and only its inner `{#key tab.id + '|' + tab.path + '|' + reloadVersion}` (NoteEditor.svelte:773) tears down. `tab` is a live `$props()` getter, so by the time NotePane's `onDestroy` → `doFlush()` (NotePane.svelte:1043/368) fires with `mountedFilePath` = A's path, `tab.path` is already B's path. `handleFlush` hits `if (!filePath || filePath !== tab.path) return;` (NoteEditor.svelte:362) and returns before BOTH branches: no `saveNoteSession` for A, and no `setWriteAhead(filePath, content, cursorPos, scrollTop, …)` (line 427). NotePane's debounce timer and idle-save interval are cleared in the same onDestroy (NotePane.svelte:1031-1032), and `switchTab` (store.ts:3894) performs no flush of any kind — unlike the three departure sites (openNoteTab reuse / loadTabHistoryEntry / closeTab) which all call `flushOutgoing`. Tab A's model stays dirty with no driver. Nothing surfaces: no save-health row (no write was attempted), no journal marker, and switching back re-seeds correctly from the model via `seedBody`, so the screen looks right. The paragraph exists ONLY in the in-memory Map for the rest of the session — killed by any crash, force-quit, GPU/webview crash or power loss, with no write-ahead entry to recover from (the app's own documented recovery route). Only a graceful close (`flushAllForAppClose`) or a later departure saves it. Note the asymmetry that proves this is unintended: FocusPane captures `focusSessionId/focusSessionPath` at entry and its teardown flush (+layout.svelte:9297) therefore DOES persist on a tab switch; NotePane compares against the live tab and does not.

confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: A save failed (locked `.md` — OneDrive/Defender/Syncthing) leaving the user's paragraph only in the write-ahead net; the app is restarted and `restoreSessionTabs` seeds the tab BORN CLEAN with the recovered bytes, calling `setModelDiskBaseline(t.id, trueDisk, trueDisk !== t.content)` (store.ts:3799) which sets `netUnsaved = true` and preserves the net (PJ-207 §15). The user then deletes that note (or overwrites it via the collision dialog). `deleteWithSetting` (store.ts:5079) calls `preserveWorkBeforeVacating`, whose filter is `isGone(t.path) && isNoteDirty(t.id)` (line 5175). The recovery model is CLEAN, so `affected.length === 0` and the function returns `true` on line 5176 — "all already durable". The caller takes that as proof and runs `clearPathKeyedAuxStateOnDelete(path)` (line 5090), destroying the write-ahead entry, while `releaseTabsForVacatedPath` disposes the model (line 5237). The file that lands in `.trash` is the PRE-edit disk version. The user's unsaved work is gone from the model, gone from the net, never on disk, and the delete advertises itself as recoverable — restoring from trash silently returns the older text with no error anywhere. This is exactly the `isNoteDirty(id) || hasUnsavedRecovery(id)` pairing that `reloadTabsFromDisk` (line 1145), `adoptExternalChangeIntoTabs` (line 1350), `renameItem` (line 4870) and `NoteEditor.handleFlush` (line 427) all already apply; this one site was missed, and it is the site whose whole job is preserving work before the file leaves.
confirmed_findings.reason: Real, silent, and reachable. Verified in source: (1) store.ts:5175 filters only `isGone(t.path) && isNoteDirty(t.id)` and returns true on an empty set, while `hasUnsavedRecovery` is already imported in the same file (store.ts:18) and paired with `isNoteDirty` at 1145, 1350 and 4877. (2) The clean-but-unsaved state is genuinely produced: `restoreSessionTabs` calls `openNoteModel` (noteModel.ts:208-219 — version:0, savedVersion:0) then `setModelDiskBaseline(t.id, trueDisk, trueDisk !== t.content)` (store.ts:3806), and `setDiskBaseline` sets only `m.netUnsaved = true` (noteModel.ts:515) without touching `version`, so `isDirty` (version > savedVersion, noteModel.ts:573) is false and `hasUnsavedRecovery` (noteModel.ts:670) is true. This is the only site with that shape — the nav/open sites use `markRecoveredFromNet`, which does `m.version++`. (3) The precondition survives a restart: `setWriteAhead` persists to localStorage `constellation-wab` (store.ts:356-360) and `resolveNoteContent({preserveNet:true})` explicitly KEEPS a cid-less failed-save entry (store.ts:3122-3127) and returns `recoveredFromNet:true` (3183). (4) Both callers act on the `true`: `deleteWithSetting` (5090) and `moveToTrash` (5274) run `clearPathKeyedAuxStateOnDelete`, which `walkAuxStatePaths` (800-810) applies to `writeAheadBuffer` AND the localStorage backup — the only copy is destroyed — plus `clearSaveFailure`. (5) No self-correction: `releaseTabsForVacatedPath` calls `closeNoteModel` BEFORE `openTabs.set(survivors)` (5237-5251), so the unmounting NotePane's `handleFlush` gets `compose → {ok:false, no_model}` and returns (NoteEditor.svelte:378-380) — the `hasUnsavedRecovery` re-stash guard at NoteEditor.svelte:427 is never reached; a background restored tab has no mounted editor at all. (6) No surfaced error: `saveHealth` is an in-memory writable (store.ts:422) that does not survive the restart, so no banner exists after boot, and the `console.warn` branch cannot fire with `affected` empty. (7) Reachable from ordinary UI with no unsaved-work check: +layout.svelte:7231 (delete confirm) and :7210 (batch delete), plus the collision dialog's Overwrite via `moveToTrash`. Net effect: `.trash` receives the PRE-edit file, the recovery net is deleted, the model is disposed, and the delete advertises itself as recoverable — silent loss with no error anywhere. One correction to the candidate's implied fix: widening the filter alone is insufficient, because `flushOutgoing` short-circuits `if (!tab || !isNoteDirty(tabId)) return {ok:true}` (store.ts:690) and `noteSession.flushIfDirty` does the same (noteSession.ts:299) — a netUnsaved model would still be reported durable; the site must force a real save or return false for `hasUnsavedRecovery`. Severity MED, not app-killer: the chain requires a failed save AND a restart AND a delete/overwrite of that note before any edit re-dirties it, and the loss is bounded to that note's unsaved delta (the note itself still reaches .trash at its pre-edit version).

confirmed_findings.summary: The PJ-249 §6 index-SEEK branch of the rename cascade has no dot-directory boundary, so it rewrites .md files inside `<root>/.trash` (deleted notes) that the disk WALK it replaced skips by construction — and then re-indexes them.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: State (verified on the live universe DB, read-only): note_links holds 55 rows whose source_path is under `E:\Constellation Universes\Eisa Cognitive Knowledge\.trash\` — 18 distinct trashed notes, all 18 still present on disk — and 39 of those rows point at a LIVE note title (e.g. `ابن بطوطة`, `الأندلس`, `hajj`, `step 5 final title`). Timing: once `target_base_backfill::needs_run` returns `No` (it re-arms and completes on boot; today 7,399 rows are still NULL, so the next completed backfill arms this), `update_links_on_rename` takes the SEEK branch at libraries.rs:6728. The candidate loop at 6767-6797 filters only on `seen`-dedup, `path.exists()` (6779), the foreign-universe roots (6790) and the PJ-092 exclude set (6793). It never asks whether any path segment starts with '.', whereas both disk walkers do exactly that and call it a preserved boundary — `collect_cascade_candidates` at 7099 (`if name.starts_with('.') { continue; }`) and `collect_fresh_suspects` at 7043. So the user renames `ابن بطوطة` → `ابن بطوطة v2`; the seek returns the trashed `ابن فضلان - Copy.md`, `gate_rmw` rewrites that deleted file on disk, its path is pushed into `result.rewritten`, and the detached spawn_blocking loop at 6870 calls `reindex_single_note` on it — which has no trash guard (search.rs:12682 → index_note only checks existence + `.md`), so the deleted note's note_meta/notes_fts row is refreshed and its mtime bumped. Silence: a rewritten file is reported only in `result.rewritten` (never surfaced), `failed` is empty, the frontend toast at +layout.svelte:7462 fires only on failures, and no tab is open on a trashed path so `reloadTabsFromDisk` no-ops. The user is told the rename succeeded. Damage: (1) files the user DELETED are silently modified in place, so 'restore from trash' no longer returns what was deleted — the app's reversible-delete promise; (2) deleted notes are actively kept alive in the search index by the cascade's own reindex tail, defeating any later index cleanup; (3) the same hole applies to any dot-directory the index has rows for, not just `.trash`.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in code and against the live DB. The PJ-249 §6 SEEK branch (libraries.rs:6767-6797) filters candidates only on seen-dedup, path.exists() (6779), foreign-universe roots (6790) and the PJ-092 exclude set (6793) — it never tests for a dot-prefixed path segment, while both disk walkers it replaced do exactly that and treat it as a preserved boundary (collect_cascade_candidates:7099, collect_fresh_suspects:7043). The codebase itself declares this filter mandatory for index-derived path lists (libraries.rs:3294-3296, and has_dot_segment at 3323: "index results MUST be filtered through this to preserve the trashed/system-note exclusion invariant"); the federation boundary WAS deliberately re-applied to the seek at 6790, the dot-dir boundary was not. Live evidence (read-only copy of .constellation/search.db): note_links holds 55 rows whose source_path is under <root>\.trash\, across 18 distinct trashed notes, ALL 18 still present on disk; 39 of those rows target a LIVE note (join of target_base to note_meta.name_lower over non-trash paths: hajj, ابن بطوطة, الأندلس, بغداد, اللغة العربية, step 5 final title, +33 more). The trashed "ابن فضلان - Copy.md" (110 KB) really carries [[supports::ابن بطوطة]], [[derives-from::بغداد]], [[part-of::اللغة العربية]], so renaming any of those titles yields a changed body and gate_rmw rewrites the deleted file on disk. The detached tail at 6870-6901 then calls reindex_single_note on it; index_note_impl (search.rs:7884) gates only on exists() + ".md" with force:true, so a .trash note is handed to the indexer — the exact thing the test at libraries.rs:7439 asserts must NEVER happen — refreshing its note_meta/FTS row and bumping its mtime against later cleanup. Silence is complete: the path lands only in result.rewritten, failed stays empty, the frontend (+layout.svelte 7479-7554) only reloads tabs and re-fetches the graph, and no tab is open on a trashed path — the rename reports success. Reachability is the designed steady state: needs_run returns Rearm on this DB today (7,399 NULL target_base rows, no target_base stamp in schema_versions) so it currently walks, but maybe_schedule runs the one-shot backfill in the background and stamps it, after which needs_run == No and every rename takes the seek — what PJ-249 §6 calls THE FLIP. No guard, version gate, trigger or reconcile pass prevents the disk write, and it does not self-correct. Held back from HIGH honestly: all 18 trash sources already have note_meta rows (the seek can only return paths that already have note_links rows), so the reindex tail amplifies an existing leak rather than creating new rows, and the body change is a semantically consistent link retarget — no live knowledge is lost or corrupted. The confirmed defect is the silent unauthorized write to files inside the app's reversible-delete store plus the forbidden .trash reindex. Fix shape: apply has_dot_segment in the seek loop and guard the reindex tail.

confirmed_findings.summary: The universe-switch handler clears the cockpit and Sky-View companions but not the split / dashboard-tag / index-term companions, which sit EARLIER in the render chain and so keep the previous universe's notes on screen.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Universe A is active, split view is on in the main window, so the SS is rendering the Split Comparison panels for A's notes (`splitCompanionActive = true`, `splitCompanionData`, `scPanels` — SecondScreenPage:1100-1223). The user switches to Universe B. Main emits `screen:universe-switched`; the SS's u3 handler (725-758) disposes every tab model, clears `openTabs`, `peekTab`, `editorPanelsActive/Data`, `skyviewNode`, `pinnedSkyviewNode` and `allNotes`, then reloads. It never touches `splitCompanionActive`, `splitCompanionData`, `scPanels`, `dashboardMode`/`dashboardTagNotes`, or `indexMode`/`indexTermData`/`indexCompareData`. Those three branches are tested BEFORE `editorPanelsActive` in the `{#if}` chain (1025 / 1047 / 1069 / 1100 vs 1225), so they win the screen: the second monitor goes on showing Universe A's note names, properties, tags and backlinks — sourced from `scPanels`, built from A's `note.content` snapshots — while Universe B is the active universe. Main only re-pushes `emitSplitModeChanged` when `$splitActive`/`$openTabs` next change (+layout:769-787), so if the user simply looks at screen 2 after switching, the wrong universe's knowledge stays displayed with no cue. This is exactly the defect PJ-207 §15 fixed for the cockpit (see the comment at 742-746); the fix was not carried to its three siblings.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in source. SecondScreenPage.svelte:725-758 (u3 `screen:universe-switched`) clears tabs, peek, cockpit (`editorPanelsActive/Data`), Sky-View (`skyviewNode`/`pinnedSkyviewNode`/history), `allNotes` and the link-type vocabulary — but never `dashboardMode`/`dashboardTagNotes` (81-83), `indexMode`/`indexTermData`/`indexCompareData` (86-88), or `splitCompanionActive`/`splitCompanionData`/`scPanels` (75-76, 182). Those three branches sit EARLIER in the `{#if}` chain (1025 / 1047 / 1069 / 1100) than the cockpit branch PJ-207 §15 did fix (1225), so they win the screen. No spinner masks it: loadAllData (474-494) raises `loading` only when `!initialLoadDone`. Main never re-pushes or clears them: emitDashboardTagSelected / emitIndexTermSelected / emitIndexCompare fire ONLY on a user click in main (+layout 9596 / 8678 / 8689) and switchUniverse (3100-3229) emits none of them — so the dashboard/index companions have NO clearing path at all. For split, the sync $effect (+layout 769-787) is `if (active && tabs.length>0) emit else if (!active) emit(false)`; switchUniverse's flushDisposeClearTabs (store.ts:3510-3522) empties openTabs but never sets splitActive false, so the effect re-runs with active=true / tabs=0 and falls through BOTH branches — no emit, stale panels retained (self-corrects only if the new universe's session restore appends >=1 tab, store.ts:3817-3823; a new/empty universe restores nothing). Concrete failure: in Universe A the user clicks a Dashboard tag, SS shows "#tag - N notes"; he switches to Universe B; SS retitles to B and reloads B's notes yet keeps rendering A's note names and A's library colours indefinitely, silently, with no error or cue, until he clicks the SS back arrow or fires another event on main. The split branch adds a live stale-path action surface: its retained rows call sendNoteToMain / showSSNoteMenu with Universe A absolute paths, and main dispatches `screen:request-note-action` straight into handleOrgNodeMenuAction (rename/move/delete) with no active-universe validation (+layout 3968-3971) — the exact harm the PJ-207 §15 comment at 742-746 names, left unfixed for the cockpit's three siblings.

confirmed_findings.summary: `retrySaveFailure` writes the note durably to disk but never emits `screen:note-saved`, so the second screen keeps rendering the pre-edit body of the very note whose save had been failing.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: A note is open in a main-window tab AND in a second-screen tab (or its peek pane). The `.md` is briefly locked (AV scan / sync), so the debounced save fails: the model stays dirty, the write-ahead net is retained and the save-health banner appears. ~10 s later the auto-retry timer (+layout:1761-1767) calls `retrySaveFailure`, which runs `saveNoteSession(... standardSaveEnv({ origin:'retry_save', onSaved: reindexNote }))` — note the `onSaved` callback contains ONLY `reindexNote`; unlike NoteEditor's four save sites (NoteEditor:266/320/441/584) and `navFlushEnv` (store.ts:652) it does not broadcast. The write goes through the gate, which suppresses the watcher, so no `library-changed` fires either, and a rename cascade is not involved so no `cascade:rewrote` fires. Result: disk and the main window now hold the new text, the search index is current, the banner clears — and the second screen's tab still shows the pre-failure body indefinitely, with its model's `diskBaseline` frozen at the old bytes. Nothing surfaces; the only thing that ever repairs it is an unrelated later save of the same note. `navFlushEnv`'s own doc comment (store.ts:641-646) states this exact hazard — 'A bare flush omits the onSaved side effects, which would leave ... the second screen un-notified' — and it was fixed for the nav-flush path only; `retry_save`, `rename_flush` (4794), `move_flush` (4953), `cid_ensure_flush` (3646) and `flushOpenTabOrAbort` (1763) all still use the bare env.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified at src/lib/libraries/store.ts:520-531: retrySaveFailure's onSaved is `void reindexNote(...)` alone — no `emit('screen:note-saved')` and no `reembedNote`, unlike every other durable-save site (NoteEditor handleSave/stage_promote, navFlushEnv store.ts:652, focus_pane +layout:1794, store.ts:1868/6166). The retry write goes through write_note -> write_gate::gate_write, which calls watcher_suppress::mark + mark_with_parent (write_gate.rs:256-257), so no `library-changed` reaches the second screen's u5 announce/watcher listener either, and announce_disk_write is template-only (universe.rs:2630). The SS's `screen:note-saved` handler (SecondScreenPage.svelte:673-708 -> adoptFreshDiskIntoSS) is the ONLY main->SS content-refresh channel and exists precisely to fix "SS never adopted main->SS saves". So after the ~10s auto-retry (+layout:1761-1767) persists the edit, an SS tab/peek showing that note keeps rendering the pre-edit body indefinitely with nothing surfaced; no guard prevents it and nothing schedules a repair (adoptDisk has no latch, so an unrelated later save does clear it). SEVERITY RECALIBRATED: the SS cannot cause loss — it is strictly read-only (ssReadOnly=true, SecondScreenPage:208; every NoteEditor write gated on readOnly at 208/285/361/461/541/686/803; setDisplayOnlyWindow makes flushOutgoing a no-op, store.ts:688) and SS->main carries path only (sendNoteToMain -> openNoteTab(note.path)), so disk, the main-window model and FTS5 stay correct and the harm tops out at a stale read-only view on the second monitor (LOW on its own). The MED weight comes from the co-located omission at the same line that the candidate did not claim: retry_save also omits reembedNote, and per store.ts:4128-4142 nothing ever re-embeds afterwards (constellation_search_reindex does not, index_repair.rs never touches note_embeddings, the boot backfill only covers rows that are absent) — so a note whose edit lands via the retry answers semantic search / similar-notes / CECE from its pre-edit vector permanently and silently: a genuine index<->disk divergence. One fix covers both: give retry_save the same onSaved triple navFlushEnv already has. Also verified: cid_ensure_flush (:3653), rename_flush (:4801) and move_flush (:4960) pass no onSaved at all, though rename/move at least fire cascade:rewrote, which the SS follows.

confirmed_findings.summary: The Earned-Life Ledger restore is the third writer of note_links.status, and it is the only one that does not recompute the derived rows a status flip invalidates — note_meta.incoming_* and sky_nodes.stratum/maturity are left stale with no self-heal.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Both DB-only status writers were fixed by the 2026-08-01 inspection: constellation_link_archive (search.rs:10967) and constellation_link_unarchive (search.rs:11101) each call recompute_after_link_status_change (search.rs:11025), whose own doc block states exactly why it must exist — the per-edge incoming/sky triggers are gone (MIG-079 §C.2a / PJ-066 §B4), the save-path diffs fire only on a note SAVE, and 'NO future save of the source could heal them (its captured signature already excludes archived edges, so old == new → zero recomputes)'. link_life_restore::restore builds `status = e.status.clone().unwrap_or(cur_status)` (line 321) from the ledger's retire/restore records and writes it at line 398 — and then does nothing else. Concrete state/timing: the user retires link A→B (ledger records `retire`, note_links.status='archived'). search.db is later lost/renamed-aside/rebuilt (the exact scenario MIG-104 Slice 6 exists for, per search.rs:11730's comment 'makes losing or rebuilding search.db cost nothing'). Next boot, ensure_search_db_ready spawns incoming_links_backfill::maybe_schedule (search.rs:11699) and sky_backfill BEFORE link_life_restore::maybe_schedule (search.rs:11730); index_note has re-created every link as status='active', so both backfills compute B's incoming_count / incoming_link_types / incoming_link_types_json / incoming_top_rank and both endpoints' sky_nodes.stratum + maturity COUNTING the retired edge. link_life_restore's thread then flips that row to 'archived'. The note_links_outgoing_au trigger fires (status is in its WHEN clause) so A's outgoing_* are correct — but nothing touches B's incoming_* or either sky_nodes row. derived_heal::maybe_schedule (search.rs:11744) is the only remaining converge path and it is marker-gated (derived_heal.rs:109 markers_armed); no marker is armed by a restore, so it no-ops. Result: B's backlink count and inbound type breakdown permanently overstate by one, B's Sky level/maturity are permanently wrong, and every future save of A is a no-op recompute by construction. No error is surfaced anywhere: the restore's own diag line reports the write as a success ('earned layer restored: N of M records written').
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in code: link_life_restore::restore (line 398) writes note_links.status from ledger retire/restore records (status set at link_life.rs:361-362, applied at line 318) and performs no derived recompute — run() returns immediately after restore(), and grep of the module finds no incoming/sky/converge recompute at all. Status IS an input to both uncovered families: incoming_aggregate_assignments filters nl.status != 'archived' (search.rs:2507-2511); stratum_sql_expr uses status='active' in five sub-counts (201-226); maturity_sql_expr uses status != 'archived' in all four tiers (271-309). Trigger coverage is exactly partial as claimed: note_links_outgoing_au fires on status (2319-2321) so the source's outgoing_* are correct, and note_links_sky_au fires (5564) so the sky_links EDGE is correct — but note_links_incoming_ai/ad/au are unconditionally dropped (2732-2734) and the per-edge sky stratum/maturity triggers are unconditionally dropped (5871-5873, 5927-5929, PJ-066 §B4). The surviving sky-node triggers fire only WHEN note_meta.word_count (5899) or modified/created_at (5946-5947) change; the outgoing trigger's note_meta write touches neither, so neither fires. No self-heal: derived_heal returns early unless markers_armed (derived_heal.rs:109-123) and a restore arms no marker; the only converge_derived_views entry points are after_repair_run (user-invoked), heal_interrupted_walk (marker-gated), after_mig108, after_vocabulary_change, after_incoming_backfill — reconcile calls none. The save path cannot heal it, and I verified the premise rather than trusting the comment: link_row_is_preserved (477-489) preserves status != 'active' across a re-index, so a later save of the source re-inserts the edge still archived, incoming_signature old == new, and maintain_incoming_after_save / maintain_sky_after_save compute an empty affected set; index_note's note_meta UPSERT (8167-8184) excludes incoming_* from its SET list so the target's stale count survives its own re-index. Deterministic reachable timing without any race: constellation_link_archive fsyncs the ledger record FIRST (10949-10954) and writes the DB only afterwards (10958), so a crash/kill in that window leaves ledger='archived' / DB='active'; the next boot's deliberately unstamped restore flips the row long after incoming_links_backfill and sky_backfill have stamped and can never run again. The MIG-104 headline path gives the same result: boot N rebuilds the index (restore reports index_not_ready while the backfills complete and stamp), boot N+1 the restore flips every retired edge. Result: the target's incoming_count / incoming_link_types / incoming_link_types_json / incoming_top_rank and both endpoints' sky_nodes.stratum + maturity count an edge that is archived, while the live getBacklinks list excludes it — badge and list disagree with no error surfaced; the restore's own diag line reports success. One correction to the candidate's wording: 'permanently' is an overclaim — maturity self-heals on any later save of the target (modified changes), stratum when word_count changes, and incoming_* if any note later adds/removes a link resolving to that target (absolute recompute); the defect is that nothing guarantees or schedules any of those. Source of truth (.md files) and note_links itself are intact, so this is derived-index divergence, not data loss — the identical class the 2026-08-01 inspection confirmed and fixed at the other two status writers (search.rs:10968, 11105 calling recompute_after_link_status_change), missed at this third one. Fix: collect the (source_path, target_lower) pairs whose status actually changed and call recompute_after_link_status_change for each after the batches commit.

confirmed_findings.summary: Canvas "promote to note" builds frontmatter by raw interpolation — `canvas_origin: "${canvasTitle}"` plus an unquoted `canvas_quadrant: ${item.quadrant}` — with no escaping, so a canvas title containing a quote emits unparseable frontmatter into a brand-new note.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Name a Sense-Making Canvas `My "Canvas"` and promote any card to a note. Line 341 emits `canvas_origin: "My "Canvas""`. Verified with the app's `yaml` parser: 1 error, `Unexpected scalar at node end at line 1, column 21`. `createNote` → `writeNote('canvas_export')` → `reindexNote` all succeed silently and the note opens normally, but its frontmatter is permanently unrewritable (H1 passthrough), so `stage`, tags, and every later property edit on that note are silently dropped. Same emitter, same missing `quoteIfNeeded` as ExpressionForge:139.
confirmed_findings.reason: Real, reachable, silent. VERIFIED IN CODE: (1) SenseMakingCanvas.svelte:341 interpolates canvasTitle into `canvas_origin: \"${canvasTitle}\"` with no escaping, while the codebase's own PJ-187 quoter `quoteIfNeeded` (store.ts:2791, exported precisely because other sites hand-built frontmatter lines and emitted invalid YAML) is not called. (2) The title is free user text and survives unescaped: createNewCanvas sets canvasTitle = newCanvasName.trim(), and canvas.rs::create_canvas sanitizes only the FILE NAME (`replace(['<','>',':','\"','/','\\\\','|','?','*'], \"_\")`) while storing `title: name` verbatim; openCanvas reads it back raw. (3) I ran the emitted block through the project's own `yaml` dependency: title `My \"Canvas\"` -> 1 error ('Unexpected scalar at node end'); a title containing a backslash -> 2 errors. (4) No guard: libraries.rs::write_note validates path/ADS/.md extension only, no YAML validation; createNote -> writeNote('canvas_export') -> reindexNote all resolve normally with nothing surfaced. (5) The damage is permanent: yamlDoc.ts::composeFrontmatter's H1 branch (`if (doc.errors.length) return ---rawYaml---body`) means the note's frontmatter can never be rewritten again. CANDIDATE PARTLY OVERSTATED, checked and corrected: `stage: growth` is NOT lost (the recovering parse yields stage=growth, and parseFrontmatter's line scanner projects it), and the open-editor property surface is GUARDED and VISIBLE — noteModel.ts:163 computes base.rewritable via frontmatterIsRewritable, propsAreWritable refuses the intents, and PropertyEditor.svelte:1100-1102 shows the 'could not be saved' banner. WHAT REMAINS SILENT: the closed-note tag add at +layout.svelte:7079 has no rewritable check — composeUpdatedContent hits H1, the original bytes are written back, reindexNote runs, and the handler returns true, so the tag is silently absent while success is reported; same shape for reviewer_connect (store.ts:1562) and the property half of link_mention (store.ts:1643). Trigger is narrow (a `\"` or `\\` in a canvas title) and no existing knowledge is destroyed, so this is not an app-killer, but it silently creates a permanently unrewritable note and produces a downstream false-success.

confirmed_findings.summary: `quoteIfNeeded` — the module's designated one-and-only frontmatter quoter — escapes `"` but never `\`, so any value that trips the quoting rule AND contains a backslash is emitted as a double-quoted scalar with an invalid escape sequence.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: A property value `C:\path` contains `:` → `needsQuoting` is true → line 2807 emits `"C:\path"`. Verified with the app's `yaml` parser: 1 error, `Invalid escape sequence \p`. Values with `\b`, `\t`, `\n`, `\0` are worse — they PARSE, to a silently different string (`"a\b"` → `a` + U+0008, verified). Live reach: `rebrandCopyFrontmatter` (store.ts:552 → `saveRecoveredCopy`, the last-resort rescue file the user makes when their note is locked — a broken title lands on the one file being rescued), and the new-note template merge (+layout.svelte:4802, `canonicalFields.map(p => `${p.key}: ${quoteIfNeeded(p.value)}`)`) which writes straight to disk via `write_note('template_create')`. Neither surfaces an error. The correct escape order already exists in the codebase at `src-tauri/src/bases.rs::format_yaml_value`.
confirmed_findings.reason: Real, silent, reachable. `quoteIfNeeded` (src/lib/libraries/store.ts:2807) emits `\"${v.replace(/\"/g,'\\\\\"')}\"` — it escapes `\"` but never `\\`, so any value that trips `needsQuoting` AND contains a backslash becomes a double-quoted scalar with unescaped backslashes. confirmed_findings.summary: `writeCanvasNow` clears `saveDirty` AFTER its await, so a change made while a write is in flight has its dirty mark erased by that older write's completion; a flush issued before the re-armed timer fires (canvas switch, panel destroy, app-close handshake) then sees a clean canvas and writes nothing.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: `writeCanvasNow` (lines 181–191) snapshots `items` into the `invoke('write_canvas', …)` argument, awaits it, and only then executes `saveDirty = false` at line 185. Steps: the user edits a card, stops for 1 s so the debounce timer at line 196 fires and `writeCanvasNow()` starts (its payload is snapshot S1); while that IPC round-trip is in flight the user drags a card or types another character — `debouncedSave()` (line 193) sets `saveDirty = true` and arms a fresh 1000 ms timer; the in-flight write then resolves and line 185 unconditionally sets `saveDirty = false`, erasing the dirty mark for a change its payload never contained. If the user now switches canvases (`openCanvas` → `flushPendingSave`, line 205), creates a canvas (line 132), leaves the panel (`onDestroy`, line 218), or closes the app (the `pendingCanvasFlushes` handshake, line 213), every one of those paths does `if (saveTimer) clearTimeout(saveTimer)` and then `if (saveDirty) await writeCanvasNow()` — `saveDirty` is false, so the pending timer is cancelled and no write happens. The change is gone from the `.canvas` JSON on disk with `saveError` still false, so the "Could not save the canvas" banner (line 367) never appears and the UI reports a saved canvas. The fix shape used elsewhere in this codebase is the compare-and-clear (`clearNetIf`) / version-stamp idiom: only clear the flag when what was written is still what is pending.
confirmed_findings.reason:
Real, silent, and reachable — but bounded, so MED not APP-KILLER.

MECHANISM (read, not inferred). `writeCanvasNow` (SenseMakingCanvas.svelte:181–191) builds the payload `{ title: canvasTitle, items }` at line 184. I verified in Tauri 2.10's injected `scripts/ipc-protocol.js` that `processIpcMessage(payload)` (JSON.stringify) runs SYNCHRONOUSLY inside `sendIpcMessage` to materialize the `fetch` body — so the payload is a true snapshot S1 taken at invoke time, and anything mutated afterwards is not in that write. Line 185 then sets `saveDirty = false` unconditionally at promise resolution, with no compare against what was actually written.

BROKEN INVARIANT. `debouncedSave()` (193–200) is the ONLY setter and always sets `saveDirty` AND `saveTimer` together; `writeCanvasNow` clears only the flag. That makes the state "timer armed, saveDirty false" reachable — and every flush path is written on the opposite assumption: `flushPendingSave` (205–208) does `clearTimeout(saveTimer)` FIRST and only then `if (saveDirty) await writeCanvasNow()`. In the broken state it destroys the one surviving persistence path and writes nothing. All four flush entry points share it: `openCanvas` (120), `createNewCanvas` (132), `onDestroy` (215–223), and the app-close handshake (`+layout.svelte:3294`, which awaits `flushPendingCanvasSave`).

CONCRETE RECIPE. Edit a card → pause 1 s → the timer at 196 fires and `write_canvas` goes in flight (payload S1). `write_canvas` (canvas.rs:74) routes through `universe::atomic_write` (universe.rs:186): temp file + `sync_all()` fsync + rename, on top of the IPC round-trip — a window of milliseconds to tens of ms, longer under AV/sync, so it is not infinitesimal. Land one more mutation inside that window (a keystroke via `updateItemContent`, a `deleteItem` click, an `addItem` double-click, a drag's `onPointerUp`): `saveDirty` goes true and a fresh 1000 ms timer arms. The older write resolves and line 185 wipes that dirty mark. Now, with no further edit, leave within <1 s — press the × / Escape (the panel is a full-page `{:else if showSenseMakingCanvas}` block, so it unmounts immediately → onDestroy), hit Switch and pick another canvas, or close the app. The armed timer is cancelled, `saveDirty` is false, nothing is written.

SILENT + SOLE COPY. `saveError` is never set, so the "Could not save the canvas" banner (line 367) never appears, and no console error is emitted either. The `.canvas` file is that board's only store — no SQLite mirror, no note model, no session net, no `.trash` copy (canvas.rs and the component's own PJ-207 §15 comments state this). Next open silently shows the stale board.

WHY NOT REFUTED. The write is awaited and durable, but durability is not the defect — the false CLEAN is. No guard covers it: the `if (saveDirty)` gate is exactly what fails, and the timer that would have covered it is deliberately cleared first. It does not self-correct at any surfaced level. The sibling writer proves the shape is wrong here: `flushPendingSettingsSave` (store.ts:7446) uses the TIMER as the dirtiness authority (`if (!saveSettingsTimer) return`) and is structurally immune; and this codebase already named the cure — compare-and-clear `clearNetIf` (noteSession.ts:34/271), added because an in-flight save cleared a net a newer edit owned (NoteEditor.svelte:289–306). Fix shape: stamp the write (a monotonic `saveSeq`/serialized snapshot) and clear only if what was written is still what is pending, and/or make `flushPendingSave` treat an armed timer as dirty.

SEVERITY MED, not higher. Any subsequent edit re-arms `saveDirty`, and absent a flush the re-armed timer still writes correctly — so loss requires the conjunction (mutation inside the in-flight window → no further mutation → flush within <1 s). The lost delta is only what changed inside that window (one keystroke, one card add/delete, one drop position, or a promote's `[[link]]` rewrite); it is reversion, not corruption, on a secondary surface — but it is genuine, unannounced loss on a file with no second copy.

Every refutation path fails: (a) no self-correction — adoptExternalChangeIntoTabs' main-window ingress is the watcher (+layout.svelte:3736-3759) and onNoteSaved (3956), both of which drop the app's own writes via wasRecentlyWritten and Rust-side watcher_suppress::mark_with_parent (write_gate.rs:256-257); the unfiltered announce branch is emitted only by sources/mod.rs:697 and universe.rs:2639, never by an editor save; (b) no re-read on activation — switchTab (3901-3907) only flips an id and noteSession.ensure returns early on a same-path model (noteSession.ts:67-72); (c) no cross-writer serialization — saveChains is keyed by model id, not path (noteSession.ts:206); (d) the write gate does not catch it — the frontend writeNote passes no Expectation (store.ts:2906-2911), so gate_write falls to self-attestation and both twins carry the SAME cid_cn → SelfAttestedOk (write_gate.rs:407-427), so not even a would_refuse_stale journal anomaly is recorded, and the gate is SHADOW-mode anyway (437-440); (e) dirty-model guards never engage because the stale twin is CLEAN — flushIfDirty no-ops and adoptDisk's dirty-refusal is irrelevant. Severity held at LOW rather than higher only because it needs a rapid double open-in-new-tab inside the IPC window AND subsequent editing of both twins, and the duplicate is weakly visible as two identically-titled tabs; the cure is the re-check the function already performs twice.

confirmed_findings.summary: `ensure_cid_cn`'s injection branch keeps the newline that follows the opening `---` inside `fm`, so the rebuilt block gains a spurious blank line — the exact defect PJ-207 §15 stripped in `update_frontmatter_title` (which now does `strip_prefix("\r\n").or_else(strip_prefix('\n'))`), left unfixed in this sibling.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario:
Open any legacy note that has frontmatter but no `cid_cn`. `after = &content.trim_start()[3..]` begins with the newline after the opening fence, so `fm = &after[..end]` is `"
title: X"`, and line 1413's `format!("---
{}
cid_cn: {}
---{}", fm, ...)` emits `---

title: X
cid_cn: …`. On a CRLF note the same line also injects an LF-only fence into an otherwise-CRLF block. The write goes through `gate_write` and succeeds; nothing is surfaced. It is an unrequested content mutation on the note-OPEN pipeline — the same 'silent content mutation beyond what the user asked for' that `bases.rs::update_frontmatter_property` was rewritten to eliminate. YAML still parses, so the damage is a modified file (Git/Syncthing diff) rather than lost data — hence LOW.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified at src-tauri/src/canonical.rs:1408-1413 and confirmed by simulating the exact slicing. `after = &content.trim_start()[3..]` starts with the newline that follows the opening fence, so `fm = &after[..end]` is \"\\ntitle: X\" and line 1413's `format!(\"---\\n{}\\ncid_cn: {}\\n---{}\", fm, …)` emits `---\\n\\ntitle: X\\ncid_cn: …` — a spurious blank line inside frontmatter on every injection into an existing FM block (reproduced for LF, CRLF, empty-FM and leading-blank inputs). On a CRLF note the same statement writes LF-only fence and cid_cn lines into an otherwise-CRLF block (mixed EOLs), and because the branch rebuilds from `content.trim_start()` it also DISCARDS any bytes preceding the fence — precisely what the sibling `sources/mod.rs::fence_offset` doc comment forbids (\"a writer replacing one key has no business reformatting the top of the note\"). The sibling fix exists and is unpaired: libraries.rs:2190-2200 carries the PJ-207 §15 `strip_prefix(\"\\r\\n\").or_else(strip_prefix('\\n'))` naming this exact blank-line defect; commit 2edc97d7 touched canonical.rs but not this branch. Reachable and silent: `ensure_cid_cn_cmd` runs on the ordinary note-OPEN path (store.ts openNoteTab), the write goes through `write_gate::gate_write` and succeeds, and nothing is surfaced. Not refutable by a guard: no downstream normalizer removes it. Severity stays LOW, not higher: it fires ONCE per note (`content.contains(\"\\ncid_cn:\")` short-circuits thereafter, so unlike the rename sibling it cannot accumulate), the YAML still parses and `split_frontmatter`/`parse_frontmatter` read identical values, and no property, body byte, or index row is lost or diverges — the damage is a silently reformatted file (Git/Syncthing diff noise, mixed line endings), i.e. unrequested content mutation rather than data loss.

confirmed_findings.summary: `write_canvas` is a SYNC `#[tauri::command]` that performs `universe::atomic_write` — File::create + write_all + **sync_all** + rename — on the WebView2 dispatch thread. The PJ-207 §15 fix that made this write atomic did not also make it `(async)`, which every other fsync-bearing persisted-JSON save in the app carries with an explicit comment saying a sync one parks the dispatch thread.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: The Sense-Making Canvas debounces at 1000 ms (`debouncedSave`, SenseMakingCanvas.svelte:193) and fires `write_canvas` after every item drag, resize, quadrant move or text edit. Because the command is sync, each of those saves runs the `fsync` on the main thread. On a canvas stored on a network share, a USB drive, or a folder under real-time AV/sync scanning, `sync_all` blocks for 100 ms–several seconds; the whole window — every other IPC, every menu, the editor — is frozen for that duration, once per second of canvas work. Same one-word omission applies to `save_app_prefs` (app_prefs.rs:54) and `save_style_presets` (style_presets.rs:44), which also fsync synchronously, and to the read commands `read_universe_settings` (universe.rs:1655), `read_universe_workspaces` (:1737), `read_universe_collections` (:1864) and `read_universe_property_types` (:1923), whose own doc comments claim they were made `(async)` in Batch-S but which are all still plain `#[tauri::command]` — with `read_universe_collections` additionally able to perform a full fsync-bearing `atomic_write` (the legacy workbench.json adoption at :1884) on the main thread.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified by reading the code. `write_canvas` (src-tauri/src/canvas.rs:73-98) is a plain `#[tauri::command]` — no `(async)` — registered at lib.rs:563, and it calls `crate::universe::atomic_write` (universe.rs:186-212) which performs File::create + write_all + **sync_all** + rename, preceded by `validate_path_in_any_library` (libraries.rs:653, canonicalize per library). Tauri executes non-`(async)` commands on the main thread, so the fsync runs on the dispatch thread. The path is reachable and repeating: SenseMakingCanvas.svelte:193-200 is a real 1000 ms debounce driven by drag-end (:271), resize (:296), quadrant move (:310) and text edit (:362), and the surface is opened from the command palette entry `sense-making-canvas` (+layout.svelte:2573) with no feature flag. Nothing guards it. This directly violates an invariant the codebase states verbatim three times — universe.rs:1668-1675, :1750-1757, :1903-1910: "MIG-100 inspection fix (freeze class): (async) — these persisted-JSON saves now fsync (hardened atomic_write); a sync command would park the WebView2 dispatch thread for the fsync" — with save_universe_settings/_workspaces/_collections all carrying `(async)`. PJ-207 §15 introduced the fsync into write_canvas and did not add the one word, so the hazard was created by the same commit that made the invariant apply (drift class, LL-023). The identical miss is confirmed at app_prefs.rs:54 (`save_app_prefs`) and style_presets.rs:44 (`save_style_presets`), both fsync-bearing sync commands. REFUTED parts of the candidate: (a) the read commands read_universe_settings/:1737/:1923 are a single fs::read_to_string of a small JSON — no fsync, no walk, no meaningful block; the "doc comments claim (async)" point is only a stale cross-reference living inside the SAVE comments, not a defect; (b) read_universe_collections' atomic_write at :1884 is gated on `!collections.json.exists() && workbench.json.exists()`, so it can fire at most once per universe lifetime at load — not a repeatable freeze; (c) "100 ms–several seconds, window frozen once per second" is unmeasured — on local storage a small-file sync_all is single-digit ms; and (d) there is no data-loss dimension, since the write is durable and failures surface via the saveError banner + prefixed console.error (SenseMakingCanvas.svelte:187-190).

confirmed_findings.summary: `create_note` never calls `ensure_search_db_ready`, so a note created during the cold-boot window is written to disk with no `note_meta` row at all and the failure is only diag_logged.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: In the 20–40 s cold-init window the user creates a note. `gate_create_exclusive` writes the .md (watcher-suppressed). The synchronous reindex at libraries.rs:1336 — which the MIG-099 §3 comment says exists so `note_meta.name_lower` is authoritative 'the instant the file exists' — returns `Err("search DB not initialized")` and is only written to diagnostics.log; `create_note` returns the path as success. For the rest of the session that note has no index identity: it is absent from the Quick Switcher, Search Hub, the Index panel and backlink resolution, and a `[[Title]]` reference to it resolves as missing. It recovers only at the NEXT boot, via `reconcile`'s re-adopt of orphan files (reconcile.rs:552-570) — and only if the orphan set is under the cap, above which re-adopt is skipped entirely.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified at libraries.rs:1322-1348 — create_note contains no ensure_search_db_ready call, catches reindex_single_note's Err and writes it only to diag_log, then returns Ok(path). The cold-init window is real and measured: ensure_search_db_ready (search.rs:11476) publishes state.db only AFTER init_db returns, and cache.rs:167 documents the 20-40s cold init that the boot commands were made (async) to survive — so state.db is None for that whole span while the UI stays interactive. reindex_single_note (search.rs:12770-12782) returns Err in that state, so the note lands on disk with no note_meta row and nothing user-visible says so. The in-code justification at libraries.rs:1319-1321 ("the watcher / next open re-indexes") is false on BOTH counts: gate_create_exclusive -> atomic_write calls watcher_suppress::mark + mark_with_parent (write_gate.rs:256-257) so no library-changed event fires, and openNoteTab's only reindex (store.ts:3338) is gated on !extractCidCn(content), which can never be true for a note create_note already stamped with cid_cn at libraries.rs:1284. It is also the one write-path command left un-ensured after the 2026-08-01 inspection hardened its siblings for this exact window — move_item refuses up front (libraries.rs:2554), constellation_search_reindex is ensure-first (search.rs:12262), rename_item ensures at 1598/1639. Severity stays LOW: the .md on disk is correct and durable, the first ordinary save heals it via the ensure-first constellation_search_reindex within ~1.5s, reconcile re-adopts the orphan at next boot (reconcile.rs:552-570), and PJ-207's drift report survives even a cap abort (reconcile.rs:398-417) so residual divergence is surfaced. Exposure is bounded to a note created inside the boot window and never edited — absent from Quick Switcher, Search Hub, Index and backlink resolution for that session — plus the narrower MIG-099 §2 consequence that a second divergent-title create in the same window escapes the index-backed duplicate-title check. Fix is a one-line ensure_search_db_ready(&app) before the reindex block.
